newsitem.title: UK: C&W jumps but eyes remain on China, alliance.
newsitem.headline: C&W jumps but eyes remain on China, alliance.

text.p: Shares in Cable and Wireless Plc jumped 16p to 502p by 0930 GMT on Wednesday, helped by a strong overnight performance from its biggest asset -- Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd.
Simon Carrington, telecoms analyst at brokers Merrill Lynch, said the shares were finding support at 500p, after a recent bout of underperformance.

But he added that the stock was unlikely to climb much higher unless C&W strikes a deal with China, links up with a global alliance, or there is the prospect of further earnings enhancing disposals this year.

Hong Kong Telecom shares rose to new year-highs of HK$17.70 overnight, amid a buying spree sparked by renewed talk that C&W was poised to sell down its near-60 percent stake to mainland Chinese investors.

Analysts are split about whether to believe C&W's denials that it is under pressure to sell its lucrative holding in a move expected to be reciprocated with growth opportunities on the booming Chinese mainland.

Few expect the company to give up majority control without a fight but China is seen building its 7.7 percent stake in the Hong Kong company to at least 10 percent so it can claim a seat on the board.

A C&W company spokeswoman said only: "We've always maintained our line that as far as we're concerned, we will always act commercially and in the best interests of our shareholders and customers. We're not compelled to do anything. But neither do we make predictions about market sensitive issues."

Merger talks between America's AT & T Corp and SBC Communications Inc also helped the stock, making one of C&W's potential alliance partners more attractive. But analysts said a merger would at best face an uphill struggle for U.S. regulatory clearance.
C&W has said it is in alliance talks with groups such as AT&T and the Global One partnership of Deutsche Telekom AG, France Telecom and Sprint Corp.

Any deal between AT&T and SBC would give AT&T back a commanding presence in key local markets in the world's biggest telecoms market -- and boost its wireless subscriber base in seven of the top 10 major U.S. metropolitan markets.

And with the privatisation of France Telecom shrouded in uncertainty if the French Socialists win the election, the Global One tie-up may no longer be C&W's best- placed alliance partner, analysts said.

"If privatisation does not (go ahead), we've suddenly got a position where Global One is effectively emasculated and won't be able to conduct busines in the way that it is expected to," said Andrew Moffatt, telecoms analyst at SocGen.
"If that happens, then I think you'll see C&W suddenly start to consider its options."

Analysts say that although the French Socialists may be opposed to selling off state-owned assets, they may be forced by economics and possibly by EU liberalisation directives into a limited privatisation programme if they win a parliamentary majority in elections on Sunday.
